title: thread-condensation-lab-notes
summary: Personal lab notes exploring an approach to condense multi-turn conversation threads into compact representations for cheaper retrieval, faster context restoration, and UX previews. Rough user stories, technical options, metrics, and an experiment plan.
content:
(scratchpad) Thread condensation — lab notes

Motivation:
- Many customers keep long chat histories and feed them as context for follow-ups; token costs and latency blow up.
- Idea: produce a compact, fidelity-weighted representation of a conversation thread that preserves intent, entities, and key facts while dropping verbatim fluff. Use when recovering context for new turns or for retrieval.

Problem statement (quick):
- Given a multi-turn thread (N messages, variable length), produce a condensed artifact (~X tokens) that: preserves safety-critical facts (PII, consent flags), retains actionable state (open tasks, preferences), and is easy to rehydrate or reference at query-time.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce average context tokens used per recovery by 4x for typical threads (~20-80 turns).
- Maintain downstream model QA/assistant accuracy within 3% of full-history baseline on core tasks (slot-fill, clarification, instruction-following).
- Show clear cost delta: tokens saved -> $/1000 requests.

User stories (raw):
- As a product user, I want my assistant to "remember" the gist of prior convo without re-sending the whole transcript so responses are fast and cheap.
- As a developer, I want an API to request a condensed thread with tunable fidelity/length budget, plus ability to fetch original transcript if needed.
- As an admin, I want to audit condensed artifacts for privacy and revert to raw transcript when required.

Acceptance criteria (rough):
- API call condense_thread(thread_id, budget=256, keep_entities=true) returns artifact + provenance.
- Console shows condensed preview vs. original; user can expand collapsed segments.
- On holdout eval, assistant using condensed context answers >=97% of slot-fill queries compared to full history baseline.

Potential condensation strategies (brain dump):
1) Summarization-based (L2 summarize, L3 compress):
   - Multi-pass: first generate turn-level bullet points, then synthesize to a single compact summary.
   - Pros: easy to implement, interpretable.
   - Cons: hallucination risk; needs QA/evals.

2) Embedding-anchored extractive skeletons:
   - Compute embeddings for turns; cluster semantically; keep representative spans.
   - Pros: preserves exact spans for critical phrases (names, tokens).
   - Cons: harder to produce concise human-readable artifact; retrieval mismatch risk.

3) Hybrid: entity-first extraction + abstractive glue:
   - Extract canonical entities (people, dates, numbers, preferences) and create a short narrative stitching them in context.

4) Delta KV snapshots (session-state model):
   - Convert thread into a small set of key-value pairs representing current state (open_bugs, user_prefs, outstanding_actions).
   - Pros: super compact, structured; great for programmatic uses.
   - Cons: requires schema design and may miss nuance.

5) Smart token-preserving compression (lossy encoder):
   - Use lightweight compression hints: keep first mention + last mention, collapse repeated confirmations.

Heuristics/constraints to keep in artifact:
- Always preserve explicit consent / legal flags.
- Always preserve explicit account identifiers or pointers (IDs) unless redaction requested.
- Keep latest N system messages verbatim (maybe 2).
- Respect customer-configured redaction/privacy toggles.

Privacy and compliance thoughts:
- Condensed artifacts are derivative user data; must obey retention and KMS rules like other transcripts.
- Add metadata: source-message-ids (or ranges), checksum, model-version that produced condensation.
- Consider option to store only encrypted condensed artifacts (default for Private/Dedicated).

API sketch (very rough):
- POST /v1/threads/{id}/condense body: {budget_tokens:int, strategy:string ("hybrid"|"kv"|"extractive"), retain_entities:[str], redact_pii:bool}
- Response: {condensed_text:string, tokens_saved:int, provenance:[str], quality_score:float}

Console UX ideas:
- "Condensed view" toggle in thread history with side-by-side diff and expandable segments.
- Preview quality badge (auto-eval quick metric) and "regenerate" button with different budget.
- Allow workspace admins to set default condensation policy per app.

Evaluation plan / experiments:
- Phase 0: Data collection. Sample 2k threads from hosted API (opt-in/anon) across domains: support chats, planning threads, long-form brainstorming. Label 200 threads with gold QA (slot-fill, follow-up accuracy).
- Phase 1: Implement prototype hybrid summarizer using existing hosted model (curie/xx-small) -> evaluate fidelity vs tokens.
- Phase 2: Run A/B tests: baseline (full-history) vs condense-256 vs condense-128 for latency, cost, quality on small customer cohort.

Metrics to track:
- tokens_per_request (pre/post), tail latency (p90,p99), cost_per_1k_requests, downstream-quality-f1 on labeled tasks, regeneration_rate (how often users request raw history).

Rollout considerations:
- Start as opt-in feature for Hosted API with workspace-level toggle.
- For Dedicated/Private, expose condense as library code customers can run locally (no server artifact stored by Redwood unless requested).

Open questions / risks (notes to self):
- How to guarantee non-hallucination for facts? Do we force extractive copy for entity-rich content and abstractive glue only for non-factual fluff?
- Performance: condensation itself is compute; must be cheaper than cost saved for common patterns. Need microbenchmarks.
- UX expectations: will users accept "approximate memory" vs verbatim recall? We need clear UI affordances.
- Data lifecycle: how long to keep condensed artifacts? sync with transcript retention.

Next steps (todo):
- [ ] Add stub API spec in product backlog (JIRA-INF-4321).
- [ ] Prototype hybrid condense flow (Riya + Omar) — target 2-week spike.
- [ ] Pull sample threads for Phase 0 eval (ask Analytics for anonymized dump).
- [ ] Draft console mockups for condensed toggle (Lin to sketch).
- [ ] List required SRE/infra changes for storing encrypted condensed blobs.

Quick notes / random thoughts:
- Could pair condensation with embedding cache: condensed artifact -> embedding -> cheap rerank for retrieval.
- Consider "condense-on-idle": background condense when thread goes quiet for X hours to avoid blocking hot paths.
- Potential productized variant: "summarized-memories" as a paid opt-in with retention window and audit logs.

Reference checklist before sharing with PMs:
- concrete API proposals, privacy review, rough cost model, sample eval results (>=500 threads), console mockups.

-- end scratchpad --

Notes to self: keep this lightweight. Will rework into PRD outline if spike returns promising metrics.
